extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting preprints in the medical, clinical, and related health sciences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for depositing preprints on medRxiv, including what manuscript types are allowed, formatting and file requirements, ethical and reporting obligations, data-sharing expectations, and policies on revisions/withdrawals. Intended to govern submission and basic screening prior to posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject scope eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript must concern a relevant scientific field in the medical, clinical, and related health sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: medRxiv is an archive for preprints in the health sciences; submissions outside these fields are inappropriate and may be declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Original research articles, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, data articles, and articles describing methodological research/investigations or clinical research design protocols may be posted on medRxiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are considered appropriate content for medRxiv postings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative reviews and hypotheses, case reports, editorial/commentary/opinion articles, correspondence relating to articles elsewhere that does not itself include new research, and laboratory protocols that are not themselves part of a research paper being submitted to medRxiv are not appropriate and will be declined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not submit these types of documents as standalone preprints to medRxiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint posting exclusivity and prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript may be submitted prior to, or concurrently with, submission to a journal but will not be posted if it has already been accepted for publication, published, or posted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not deposit manuscripts that have already been accepted/published or that have been posted elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author consent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript may be deposited in medRxiv provided that all its authors have consented to its deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all co-authors agree to deposition before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to deposit preprints must first register on the site. There is no charge for registration or manuscript deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an account on medRxiv; submission is free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic screening for content and health risk
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts uploaded to medRxiv undergo a basic screening process for offensive and/or non-scientific content and for material that might pose a health risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts are not peer-reviewed before posting; medRxiv may decline to post submissions based on this screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to decline posting
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv reserves the right to decline to post any preprint for any reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting is discretionary; lack of posting does not imply journal peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript file format — single PDF preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplest way to deposit a manuscript on medRxiv is to upload a single PDF including the text and any figures/tables. All manuscripts should include the title, author names and affiliations, and abstract on the title page. Supplemental data should be created in a separate file or files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the PDF contains title page information and that supplemental materials are separate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate upload formats and conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: You may upload a Word file containing the main text (plus any tables) and separate figure files, from which a single PDF will be created by an automated PDF-conversion engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conversion engine accepts many figure formats (JPEG, TIFF, EPS, PowerPoint) but not PICT, Bitmap, Excel, PSD; convert incompatible files to PDF or acceptable formats. LaTeX files should be converted to PDF prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material allowed and large-data deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are free to include Supplemental Material such as additional tables and MPEG files. Large datasets, however, should be deposited in the appropriate scientific community database (e.g., clinical trial data sharing sites, PDB, GenBank, NIH sites such as BioLINCC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large datasets use community repositories; link to those datasets from the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data use and acknowledgment standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should abide by all relevant community guidelines for use and acknowledgment of data resources (e.g., the Fort Lauderdale guidelines), obtaining permission where required and citing the appropriate laboratory, website, and accession numbers, including clinical trial registration information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite accession numbers and provide permissions as needed; include trial registration info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At submission authors must include a statement regarding the availability of all data referred to in the manuscript, along with links to any data hosted in an external repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear data availability statement and URLs/accession numbers for external datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and approvals declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should declare at submission that all relevant ethical guidelines have been followed, all necessary IRB and/or ethics committee approvals have been obtained, all necessary patient/participant consent has been obtained and the appropriate institutional forms archived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statements and archive forms showing ethics committee approvals and consenting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any clinical trials described should be registered with an internationally recognized trial registry and the trial ID included in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include trial registry identifier(s) in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interest and funding statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include a competing interest statement, including explicit acknowledgment of whether the authors or their institutions received any payments or services in the past 36 months from a third party that could be perceived to influence the submitted work. Authors should also provide a funding statement with details of all funding that supported the work presented, including explicit acknowledgment of whether the authors or their institutions at any time received payment or services from a third party for any aspect of the submitted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose conflicts of interest and all sources of funding, including payments that could be perceived as influencing the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of distribution and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: After a manuscript is deposited in medRxiv, it is citable and cannot be removed. The copyright remains with the author, who is asked to select from several distribution/reuse options (CC BY, CC BY-NC, CC BY-ND, CC BY-NC-ND, CC0, or no reuse). By posting on medRxiv, authors consent to text mining of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an appropriate license at submission; understand that posting makes the work citable and accessible for text-mining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal and plagiarism/ethics enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv reserves the right to identify and remove any preprints for any reason, and in particular preprints that contain plagiarized material or describe experimental work that is not performed in accordance with the relevant ethical standards for research using animals or human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure originality and adherence to ethical standards to avoid removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are free to submit a revised version of a manuscript at any time (prior to acceptance at a journal) by clicking on 'Submit a revision' within the Author Area. The new version will use the same DOI as the original submission, which also will remain accessible on the medRxiv site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmit supplemental files if they change; if no changes to supplemental data, resubmission of those files is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawals policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may request to have their manuscript marked as 'Withdrawn' if they no longer stand by their findings/conclusions or acknowledge fundamental errors in the manuscript. In these cases, a statement explaining the reason for the withdrawal is posted on the medRxiv manuscript page to which the DOI defaults. The original manuscript is still accessible via the Info/History tab on medRxiv. In extremely rare, exceptional cases, preprints may be removed for legal reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal marks remain visible and the original content remains accessible in history; removal is rare and legally constrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting logistics (typesetting and order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are not typeset before being posted online. Preprints appear in medRxiv in the order in which they were approved for posting. They are retrievable via the web interface at no charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect your uploaded/manually converted PDF to be posted as-is and to appear in chronological approval order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct transfer to journals (M2J) option
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv can transmit manuscript files and metadata directly from medRxiv to participating journals (Direct Transfer from medRxiv to Journals, M2J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using M2J can save time when submitting to partner journals; a list of participating journals is provided on the site.
